title: Kanecta Auth Config API Response
description:
The wire shape returned by the PUBLIC `GET /auth-config` endpoint — the boot-time authentication configuration a browser client (Studio, an embedding app) fetches BEFORE any login to learn how to authenticate against this particular deployment.

This is what makes one built client artifact serve many deployments: instead of baking a Keycloak realm/client into the build, the client fetches this at startup and configures its OIDC login from whatever the deployment's API reports. A no-auth local instance and a Keycloak-protected cloud instance run the SAME build; only their API's environment differs.

The endpoint is deliberately UNAUTHENTICATED — a client cannot present a token before it knows how to obtain one. Every field here is non-secret: a public OIDC client id, the realm name, and the auth server URL are all values a browser OIDC client necessarily exposes. No secret (client secret, signing key, password) is ever part of this response.

When `authDisabled` is true the deployment runs with no Keycloak (local dev, or a single-tenant no-auth install): the client initialises no OIDC layer and sends no Authorization header, matching the API's AUTH_DISABLED bypass. When false, the client uses `keycloakUrl` + `realm` + `clientId` to drive the login flow.

authDisabled.description: True when this deployment runs with authentication disabled (the API's AUTH_DISABLED bypass). The client then initialises no Keycloak and sends no token. When true, `keycloakUrl`, `realm`, and `clientId` are null.

keycloakUrl.description: Base URL of the Keycloak server the client should authenticate against (e.g. 'https://auth.example.com'), or null when `authDisabled` is true. Non-secret — a browser OIDC client redirects here in the open.

realm.description: Keycloak realm the client logs in to, or null when `authDisabled` is true. Non-secret.

clientId.description: The PUBLIC OIDC client id the browser client presents when logging in, or null when `authDisabled` is true. This is a public client (no client secret); the id is not sensitive.
